defect_and_fix.defect: src/db/registry-digest-dao.ts, function pickSampleValue: the per-record 'sample' value shown to the assistant's LLM context was the FIRST scalar in record.data's key-insertion order, with no regard for what that field IS. For a registry whose record_schema lists a code/number-shaped field before its actual name field, the digest showed the code as if it were the record's human-readable title (LIVE_PROOF T-0607: an ИНН value surfaced instead of an organisation name).
defect_and_fix.fix: New pure, IO-free module src/core/registry-title-field.ts exports pickTitleFieldKey(recordSchema): resolves ONE title-field key per registry, in order: (1) an explicit record_schema['x-title-field'] annotation (forward-compatible only — nothing in the platform writes this yet); (2) a schema property whose KEY matches a small generic set of name/title-shaped spellings (English + Russian: title/name/display_name/label/наименование/название/имя/заголовок), case-insensitive; (3) the first property (schema order) whose deriveFieldType (src/core/field-type-dictionary.ts, the platform's single canonical field-type resolver) is a plain textual type ('text'/'textarea') — explicitly not number/boolean/enum/date/url/email/person/multi-select; (4) null when no candidate exists. registry-digest-dao.ts derives this key ONCE per registry (same pass that already derives numeric fields via pickNumericFieldKeys, T-0587) and pickSampleValue tries it FIRST, falling back UNCHANGED to the original data-only scan when the key is absent or blank for a given row.

reused_signal: RESEARCHED FIRST, before writing any code: no existing registry-level 'title field' signal exists anywhere in the codebase (grepped whole repo for title_field/titleField/display_field/displayField/primary_field/primaryField/label_field/labelField/x-title/x-primary/x-display against registry_def/record_schema — zero hits). The closest adjacent convention is the frontend's deriveRecordLabel (web/src/screens/records-form.js:1079, T-0447, reused by kanban's resolveCardLabel since T-0626) — but it is SCHEMA-BLIND (only ever receives record.data, never record_schema) and has the EXACT SAME defect this task closes (a code-shaped field can win purely by data-key order), so it was NOT reused as-is; copying it would have just relocated the bug. The genuinely reusable piece of infrastructure is deriveFieldType (src/core/field-type-dictionary.ts, T-0337) — already reused by the sibling pickNumericFieldKeys (src/core/visible-aggregate.ts, T-0587) inside this SAME DAO, in this SAME per-registry pass. This task's pickTitleFieldKey follows that identical pattern (one pure module, one per-registry record_schema pass, no new SQL, no new PDP path).
heuristic_order: (1) explicit record_schema['x-title-field'] string annotation naming an existing property -> wins outright (no-op today, nothing sets it yet — forward-compatible only, exercised by a unit test with a synthetic schema); (2) first property whose key normalizes (trim+lowercase) to one of: title, name, display_name, displayname, label, наименование, название, имя, заголовок; (3) first property (schema property order) whose deriveFieldType resolves to 'text' or 'textarea'; (4) null — caller (pickSampleValue) falls through UNCHANGED to the pre-existing generic data-scan (first non-empty string scalar by key order, then any scalar).
backward_compatibility: Additive/non-breaking: ReadableRegistryEntry's shape (samples: string[]) is unchanged. A registry whose schema has no title-field candidate at all (e.g. all-numeric/all-enum schema, or no record_schema) produces byte-identical digest output to pre-T-0613 behaviour — verified by unit tests (registry-title-field.test.ts: 'only a numeric field' / 'only enum/boolean/date-shaped fields' -> null) and by pickSampleValue's explicit fallthrough for a blank/missing value under the resolved key.

tests_added.covers: 13 pure unit tests, zero IO: (a) code-shaped field BEFORE a name-like field -> name wins (the exact regression shape from LIVE_PROOF T-0607, using generic 'code'/'name' fixture keys, no business-domain literal); (b) numeric field before a name-like field -> name still wins (step 2 fires before step 3 inspects types); (c) no name-like key present -> falls back to first plain-textual field, skipping an earlier numeric field; (d) Russian name-like key recognized generically (наименование); (e) case-insensitive key matching; (f) only a numeric field (no textual field at all) -> null; (g) only enum/boolean/date-shaped fields -> null; (h) empty properties -> null; (i) explicit x-title-field wins over both other guesses; (j) x-title-field pointing at a non-existent key or non-string value is ignored (falls through); (k) malformed/absent schema (null/undefined/non-object/missing properties/non-object properties) -> null, never throws; (l) a malformed individual property definition is skipped, not thrown on.

New DB-level regression test (live Postgres): a registry whose record_schema has a code-shaped field ('code') BEFORE a name field ('name') in property order, with a seeded record populating both — loadReadableRegistryDigest's sample for that record is the name value ('Тестовая запись'), and explicitly NEVER contains the code value ('7701234567'). All 3 pre-existing scenarios in this file (AC-3a/AC-3b owner-vs-non-reader, T-0587 narrow-grant subset, adversary-honesty truncation) left completely unmodified and still pass.

live_proof.summary: Asked the assistant chat 'Покажи поставщиков' about a newly created, published registry ('T0613 LP Поставщики' / 'Поставщики', slug postavshiki) whose schema places a code-shaped field (inn/ИНН) BEFORE its name field (name/Наименование) — the exact anti-case shape from LIVE_PROOF T-0607. The assistant's verbatim answer named both records by their display name ('АО Василёк', 'ООО Ромашка'), never by their ИНН code (7798765432 / 7712345678), which was only offered as an optional follow-up detail. Cross-checked via SQL that the registry_def.record_schema JSON key order is genuinely inn-then-name and the record data matches.
live_proof.workarounds: None in the proof itself (case creation + assistant question all via UI clicks/forms); SQL used only as a cross-check of schema key order, not as a substitute for the UI observation.
